checkpoints.prompt: Your MCP server is at https://mcp.<yourname>.example/mcp. (1) Who is the resource owner, the client, the authorization server, and the resource server? (2) Which of them may hold a client secret, and why can the others not? (3) An attacker reads your browser history and finds ?code=…. What else do they need, and where does it live?

Four tokens arrive at your MCP server. For each, give the HTTP status and name the check that decided. (1) Signature valid, iss correct, aud = your web API, exp in 12 min. (2) Signature valid, aud correct, scope = 'openid profile', no campuspulse.* scope. (3) alg: none, payload says roles:[operator], no signature segment. (4) Signature valid, everything correct, exp was 90 seconds ago, configured skew is 60s.

Write the scope-to-tool policy table for YOUR OWN MCP server, including a row for the default. Your tools are list_service_status (read), get_incident (read), post_incident_update (writes), and delete_incident (destructive, shipping tomorrow). (1) Which scopes exist and which tool needs which? (2) delete_incident ships tomorrow and nobody updates the table — what happens, and what should happen?
